packages.desc: Actual Budget, private envelope budgeting that syncs between your devices, in Container Manager — with your budgets kept on your Synology, and a DSM window for the server password (shown once), signing every device out, a warning when your devices stop syncing, HTTPS with DSM's certificate (Actual needs HTTPS), backups and updates.
packages.changelog:
First release. Actual Budget's server in Container Manager, on HTTPS from the start: DSM's certificate, or a self-signed one when there isn't one. Plain HTTP is allowed only behind DSM's reverse proxy. The server password is set at the first start and shown once.

The DSM window adds:
• Budgets: each budget's size, last sync, and whether it's encrypted or deleted; the devices signed in; a DSM notification when syncing goes quiet; and the upload size limit.
• Sign-in: a QR code for phones, a new password (optionally signing every device out), and sign every device out.

Also included: consistent backups, updates and removal.

packages.desc: Audiobookshelf, your own audiobook and podcast server, in Container Manager — streaming the books and podcasts in your shared folders to the web and to its phone apps, with listening progress kept in sync, and a DSM window for libraries and scans, users, phone setup with a QR code, backups and updates.
packages.changelog:
First release. Audiobookshelf 2.37.1 in Container Manager:
• your audiobooks and podcasts from your shared folders: audiobooks read-only, podcasts writable for new episodes;
• your account is made at the first start, with the password shown once;
• the window works through an API key of the package's own, which it makes again by itself if it's removed in Audiobookshelf.

The DSM window adds:
• Libraries:
• books, podcasts, episodes and hours, per library and in all;
• scan one library or all, or read one again from scratch;
• add a library from a shared folder: missing folders are refused, never created;
• remove a library (its files stay);
• a folder that goes away (a USB disk, a renamed share) shows as waiting and is read again when it's back.
• Phones: a QR code, the address, and the official apps.
• Users: add people, new passwords (shown once), administrator on or off, remove; listening and finished counts for each.
• Updates: Audiobookshelf's newer releases, installed after a backup.

Also included: consistent backups that keep everyone's listening progress (Audiobookshelf's own backups are left alone), updates and removal.

packages.desc: BookStack, a simple wiki for documentation and how-tos, in Container Manager — with a DSM window for signing in with your Synology accounts (DSM's LDAP Server), a readable copy of the whole wiki in a shared folder, user recovery, mail settings, HTTPS with DSM's certificate, backups and updates.
packages.changelog: • The password boxes in the window (the LDAP bind password on Sign-in, the mail server's password on Mail) look like the other fields instead of small browser-default boxes.

packages.desc: Changedetection.io, the self-hosted website change monitor, in Container Manager — with a DSM window for your watches, DSM notifications and ntfy alerts when a page changes, password protection, an optional browser for JavaScript-heavy pages, backups and updates.
packages.changelog: First release. Changedetection.io 0.60.9 in Container Manager, password protection from the first start (password shown once), no example watches, and a DSM window: Watches (last change, last check and errors, with search; add a page by its address, check now, check all, pause and resume; pages on your own network on or off; the optional Chrome browser for JavaScript pages on or off), Alerts (DSM notifications for changes and failed checks, with a test; the ntfy package on this NAS connected in one click through a write-only sender; Changedetection.io's Apprise addresses listed without their secrets, added, tested and removed), Access (a new password, your own, or none), backups with restore, updates that move the pinned release on, storage, a redacted support report, and full removal.

packages.desc: DocuSeal, open-source document signing, in Container Manager — with a DSM window for what's waiting to be signed, signed copies saved to a shared folder, DSM notifications, user recovery, mail checks, HTTPS with DSM's certificate, backups and updates.
packages.changelog: First release. DocuSeal in Container Manager with SQLite behind a small nginx (HTTPS with DSM's certificate or self-signed, or plain HTTP), the administrator made at the first start through DocuSeal's own setup page (password shown once), and a DSM window: Documents (who has signed, opened or declined; filters and search), signed copies of every completed document and its audit log in the shared folder, DSM notifications for completed and declined documents, Users (new password, unlock, remove 2FA), Mail (is a mail server set up, emails sent/opened/bounced, test email), DocuSeal's own address kept in step with the Site address, consistent backups with DocuSeal's secret key, updates, storage, a redacted support report and full removal.

packages.desc: FreeScout help desk and shared mailbox, running in Container Manager, with a DSM window for password recovery, backups, mail health, updates and maintenance.
packages.changelog: • The Copy button for one-time passwords works when DSM is opened over plain HTTP (http://nas:5000), where browsers don't offer the clipboard API. If copying is refused, the password is selected with a Ctrl+C hint.

packages.desc: Homebox, the home inventory for everything you own — where it is, what it cost, its receipts, manuals and warranty — in Container Manager, with a DSM window for the people who use it (sign-ups off by default, a new password shown once), what your things are worth, a DSM notification before a warranty ends, consistent backups with every photo and receipt, and updates.
packages.changelog:
First release. Homebox 0.26.2 (the maintained sysadminsmedia fork) in Container Manager. Your account is made at the first start, with the password shown once; until it exists, Homebox answers only on the Synology itself, and sign-ups are closed afterwards.

The DSM window adds:
• Inventory: items, what they're worth, locations, attached files and warranties for every collection; the warranties ending soon; and a DSM notification a week to three months before one ends, once per item.
• Users: everyone with an account and their collections, sign-ups open or closed, and a new password (shown once) through Homebox's own password reset, which signs that person out everywhere.
• Updates: Homebox stays at a tested release; the window finds newer ones on GitHub and ghcr.io and moves to them after a backup.

Also included: consistent backups with every photo, receipt and manual, restore and removal.

packages.desc: Homepage, a start page for everything on your Synology, in Container Manager — filled in for you: DSM and its live stats, every app installed from this family of packages, and your other containers, each with up/down and response time; links of your own, a look of your choosing, and YAML you can still edit in File Station.
packages.changelog: • The DSM password box on the Synology stats tab looks like the other fields instead of a small browser-default box.

packages.desc: Immich, your own photo and video library with phone backup, in Container Manager with Postgres and Valkey — with a DSM window for photo libraries from your shared folders (read-only, scanned on demand), machine learning on or off for smaller Synologys, users and the administrator's password, phone setup with a QR code, database backups and careful updates.
packages.changelog:
First release. Immich v3.3.1 with Postgres (VectorChord) and Valkey in Container Manager, the images and versions of that release's own compose file:
• uploads go to the photos folder of the immich shared folder;
• your administrator account is made at the first start, with the password shown once;
• the package works through an API key of its own, never your password.

The DSM window adds:
• Photo libraries:
• up to five folders already on the Synology, read-only, as Immich external libraries, each in someone's timeline;
• scan one or all now; counts and the last scan;
• missing folders are refused, never created; DSM's @eaDir thumbnails are skipped;
• what's in the photos folder, and what Immich is still working on.
• Machine learning: on or off. Off frees 1–2 GB of memory on smaller Synologys; smart search and faces follow the switch. Memory in use, per container.
• Users: add people (a password shown once, their own chosen at the first sign-in), and reset the administrator's password with immich-admin.
• Phones: a QR code, the server address and the apps.

Also included: database backups as Immich documents them (pg_dump), with restore; updates that move to a newer Immich only with a package update, after backing up the database; and removal.

packages.desc: Invoice Ninja, invoicing, quotes, expenses and payments for small businesses and freelancers, in Container Manager with MariaDB — with a DSM window for what's outstanding and overdue (and a DSM notification when an invoice goes overdue), users and their passwords, the mail server that sends your invoices, HTTPS with DSM's certificate, consistent backups and updates.
packages.changelog:
First release. Invoice Ninja with MariaDB and nginx in Container Manager. Your account is made at the first start, with the password shown once; the first-start throwaway leaves the environment.

The DSM window adds:
• Business: what's owed, what's overdue and what's been paid, in each client's currency.
• Alerts: a DSM notification when an invoice goes overdue.
• Users: new passwords, and two-step sign-in off.
• Mail: the mail server, with a test email.
• Site address: HTTPS with DSM's certificate.

Also included: consistent backups, updates and removal.

packages.desc: A web-based iperf for your home network, in Container Manager: an iperf3 server on the Synology for PCs, a LibreSpeed browser test for phones and laptops, and a DSM window that runs iperf3 tests from the Synology to any device, keeps every result with a chart per device, tests on a schedule and tells DSM when the network is slower than it should be.
packages.changelog:
First release. A web-based iperf for the home network, in Container Manager: iperf3 3.20 (Alpine's, built on the Synology) as a server on port 5201, TCP and UDP, always on, and LibreSpeed 6.3.0, the browser speed test, on port 8790 — LAN only, nothing goes to the internet. The wizard suggests other ports when those are taken, and both are in DSM's firewall list.

The DSM window adds:
• Run a test: iperf3 from the Synology to any device on the network — TCP or UDP, upload, download (-R) or both, how long, parallel streams — with Mbit/s, retransmits, and jitter and packet loss for UDP. Devices can be saved with a name.
• History: every test — run here, on the schedule, from other devices against the iperf3 server, and in the browser — with a chart over time, filters per device and kind of test, and every result as a CSV.
• Schedule: an iperf3 test to one device every 15 minutes to once a day, what counts as slow, and a DSM notification when a scheduled test is slow or fails.
• How to test: the browser test's address with a QR code for phones, iperf3 commands to copy for Windows, macOS and Linux, and what limits the results.
• Site address: the iperf3 port, beside the web port.

Also included: consistent backups of the history, restore, updates (a newer LibreSpeed release, or Alpine's newer iperf3) and removal.

packages.desc: Linkwarden, bookmarks that keep a copy of each page (a screenshot, a PDF and the page itself), in Container Manager with PostgreSQL — with a DSM window for its users (new passwords, sign-ups, the administrator), the page copies kept in a shared folder and the room they take, consistent backups and updates.
packages.changelog:
First release. Linkwarden 2.16.3 with PostgreSQL 16 in Container Manager. Your account is made at the first start, with the password shown once; sign-ups are then off, and Linkwarden only listens beyond the NAS once your account exists. Linkwarden's secret is made at install and kept in the settings.

The DSM window adds:
• Users: a new password (shown once, and their old sessions signed out), sign-ups on or off, and which user is Linkwarden's administrator.
• Archive: the page copies (screenshots, PDFs, the pages themselves and their readable text) kept in the shared folder's Archive folder, how much room each kind takes, copies on or off, copies of pages on your own network, and trying the failed ones again.

Also included: consistent backups (a PostgreSQL dump and the Archive folder), updates to newer Linkwarden releases, storage, a redacted support report and full removal.

packages.desc: Memos, quick private notes you jot from any browser or phone, in Container Manager — with your notes kept on your Synology, attachments as plain files in the memos shared folder, and a DSM window for people and passwords (shown once), sign-ups, phone setup with a QR code, backups and updates.
packages.changelog:
First release. Memos 0.31 in Container Manager:
• your account is made at the first start as Memos's administrator, with the password shown once;
• sign-ups start off: only an administrator adds people;
• attached files are ordinary files in the memos shared folder, in `attachments/`;
• a package administrator handles the window's work through Memos's own API.

The DSM window adds:
• Users: everyone's memo count and last memo; add people, new passwords (shown once), administrator on or off, remove; sign-ups on or off.
• Attachments: how many files there are and how much room they take, by person; where new files go; the biggest file allowed.
• Phones: a QR code of the address, and how to put Memos on the home screen.

Also included: backups that copy the database consistently (`sqlite3 .backup`) together with `attachments/`, restore, updates and removal.

packages.desc: n8n, workflow automation — connect apps and services, run on schedules and webhooks — in Container Manager, with a DSM window that keeps its encryption key safe (in every backup, shown once when you want it), tells DSM when a workflow fails, keeps a copy of every workflow in a shared folder, manages people and passwords, and handles webhook addresses, HTTPS, backups and updates.
packages.changelog:
First release. n8n in Container Manager:
• your owner account is made at the first start, with the password shown once;
• the package has a limited API key of its own;
• the package makes the encryption key and keeps it in every backup.

The DSM window adds:
• Workflows: list, switch on and off, and runs and failures in the last 24 hours.
• Failures: DSM notifications when a workflow fails, and how long run history is kept.
• Webhooks: the address webhook URLs start with.
• Copies: a copy of every workflow in the shared folder, every 6 hours.
• Encryption key: show it once.
• People: invitation links, new passwords, two-step sign-in off, and removal.
• Site address: HTTPS with DSM's certificate, with secure cookies.

Also included: consistent backups, updates and removal.

packages.desc: Navidrome, your own music streaming server, in Container Manager — playing the music already in your shared folder to the web and to Subsonic apps on every phone, with a DSM window for the library and scans, phone setup with a QR code, users, sharing and HTTPS with DSM's certificate.
packages.changelog:
First release. Navidrome in Container Manager:
• it plays your music folder, read-only;
• your account is made at the first start, with the password shown once;
• a package administrator handles the window's work.

The DSM window adds:
• Library:
• counts and the last scan;
• scan now or read everything again, and how often to look;
• change the music folder: missing folders are refused, never created;
• songs that left the folder are counted separately;
• share links on or off.
• Phones: a QR code and recommended apps.
• Users: add people, new passwords (shown once), administrator on or off, remove.
• Site address: HTTPS with DSM's certificate.

Also included: consistent backups, updates and removal. If the music folder isn't there yet, Navidrome starts on an empty placeholder and picks the folder up when it appears.

packages.desc: ntfy, push notifications to your phone from your own server, in Container Manager — with a DSM window that sends DSM's own alerts to your phone, sets phones up with a QR code, manages users and topic access, and backs it all up.
packages.changelog: First release. ntfy in Container Manager with sign-in required, your account made at the first start (password shown once), and a DSM window: DSM's own alerts to your phone through a dedicated write-only sender and a NAS-only webhook address (copy and test), phone setup with a QR code and iOS instant delivery, users (add, new password, tokens, topic access with wildcards, remove), topics and test messages, how long messages are kept, HTTPS with DSM's certificate or self-signed, backups, updates and removal.

packages.desc: Paperless-ngx, a searchable archive for your paper — scans and PDFs are read (OCR), tagged and filed — in Container Manager with PostgreSQL, with an inbox folder in a shared folder: drop scans into paperless → Inbox. A DSM window shows what's waiting, filed and failed (and DSM tells you when a document couldn't be added), picks the OCR languages, resets passwords, adds people, keeps a readable export beside the backups, and handles updates.
packages.changelog:
First release. Paperless-ngx 3.3.0 with PostgreSQL 18 and Valkey in Container Manager. Your account, an administrator, is made at the first start, with the password shown once.

The inbox is a folder in the shared folder (paperless → Inbox):
• drop scans and PDFs in, and they're read, filed and taken out of the folder;
• a file Paperless-ngx can't add (damaged, or password-protected) is moved to Couldn't process with the reason, and DSM is told;
• Office documents and emails, through Gotenberg and Tika, when switched on (off by default, to save memory).

The DSM window adds:
• Inbox: what's waiting, what was filed, what couldn't be added, and Try again.
• OCR languages: the main language and up to five more; any of 25, the ones Paperless-ngx doesn't include installed as it starts.
• Users: add someone, new passwords (an administrator's too), two-step sign-in off, removal.
• Backups: a readable export to paperless → Export every night, beside the backups.
• Maintenance: rebuild the search index, and the sanity checker.

Also included: consistent backups, updates and removal.

packages.desc: Pi-hole, network-wide ad and tracker blocking, in Container Manager — answering DNS for every device on your network from your Synology. A DSM window shows what's blocked, pauses blocking for a while, manages blocklists and allowed or blocked sites, picks the upstream DNS, checks DSM isn't using port 53 already, and handles passwords, HTTPS, backups and updates.
packages.changelog:
First release. Pi-hole v6 in Container Manager, answering DNS on port 53. The package checks the port is free and says so if DSM's DNS Server package has it. Your password is set at the first start and shown once; the package has an app password of its own.

The DSM window adds:
• Blocking: today's figures, pause (with a timer) and resume, and the sites blocked most and just now.
• Lists: blocklists (add, remove, update), and sites always allowed or blocked.
• Setup: router steps, upstream DNS, and a new password.
• Alerts: a DSM notification when blocking is left off.
• Site address: HTTPS with DSM's certificate.

Also included: backups (with Pi-hole's own Teleporter export), updates and removal.

packages.desc: Snipe-IT, IT asset management for laptops, phones, licences and accessories, in Container Manager with MariaDB — with a DSM window for what's checked out and which warranties and licences end soon (and a DSM notification when one does), signing in with your Synology accounts (DSM's LDAP Server), users and their passwords, the mail server, HTTPS with DSM's certificate, consistent backups and updates.
packages.changelog:
First release. Snipe-IT 8.8 with MariaDB in Container Manager. Snipe-IT's web setup is done at the first start instead: its settings, the keys its API signs tokens with, and your administrator account, with the password shown once. The app key is made at install and kept in every backup.

The DSM window adds:
• Assets: how many there are, what's checked out and what's ready, licence seats in use, and which warranties, ends of life and licences end in the next 7 to 90 days.
• Alerts: a DSM notification when a warranty or licence comes that close to its end.
• Users: new passwords, two-step sign-in off, and administrator on and off (never the last one).
• Sign-in: Synology accounts through DSM's LDAP Server — a test, one switch, your account kept as administrator, and the group new people join.
• Mail: the mail server, with Snipe-IT's own test email.
• Site address: HTTPS with DSM's certificate.

Also included: consistent backups (a MariaDB dump and Snipe-IT's files), updates and removal.

packages.desc: Speedtest Tracker, which tests your internet speed on a schedule and keeps the history, in Container Manager — with a DSM window for the latest results and averages, running a test now, the schedule and server, alerts in DSM when the line is slow or a test fails, a monthly CSV of every result in a shared folder, API tokens, HTTPS with DSM's certificate, backups and updates.
packages.changelog:
First release. Speedtest Tracker in Container Manager. Its default admin@example.com / password login is replaced by your account at the first start, with the password shown once.

The DSM window adds:
• Speed: the latest results, averages over 24 hours, 7 days and 30 days, and a test on demand.
• History: a monthly CSV of every result in the shared folder.
• Schedule: how often (at this install's own minute), which server, how long results are kept, and the public dashboard.
• Alerts: thresholds, with DSM notifications for results below them and for failed tests.
• Account: a new password, and API tokens (read-only, or able to start tests), each shown once.
• Site address: HTTPS with DSM's certificate.

Also included: consistent backups, updates and removal.

packages.desc: Stirling-PDF, a toolbox for PDFs — merge, split, compress, OCR, convert, sign, redact — in Container Manager, with hot folders in a shared folder: drop scans into PDF inbox and searchable, compressed PDFs come out in PDF done. A DSM window sets up the folders and OCR languages, manages the accounts, tells you when a file couldn't be processed, and handles HTTPS, backups and updates.
packages.changelog:
First release. Stirling-PDF in Container Manager. Its default admin/stirling login becomes your account at the first start, with the password shown once.

Hot folders in the shared folder (PDF inbox → PDF done):
• Make searchable, Compress, Photos to PDF, and Clean for sharing;
• OCR in up to five languages;
• a file that still can't be processed after 10 minutes is moved aside, and DSM is told.

The DSM window adds:
• Hot folders: switch each folder on or off, see what's waiting, done and failed, the latest results, and Try again.
• Users: add, new passwords, administrator or user, removal, and a rescue administrator if you're locked out of your own account.
• Site address: HTTPS with DSM's certificate.

Also included: backups, updates and removal.

packages.desc: Technitium DNS Server in Container Manager: your own DNS server for the whole network, on your Synology. It blocks ads and trackers, answers names you give your own devices (like nas.home), and can encrypt lookups to the internet. A DSM window turns blocking on and off, manages blocklists, local names and upstream DNS, checks DSM isn't using port 53 already, and handles the password, HTTPS, backups and updates.
packages.changelog:
• DNS listens on the NAS's LAN address instead of every address. Many Synology models keep `127.0.0.1:53` for DSM itself, and 1.0.0 couldn't start alongside it ("address already in use").
• If port 53 is taken on that address, the package stops with one sentence naming what holds it, instead of retrying. The support report lists what listens on port 53.
• A Network setting on the Site address tab: the NAS's own network (new installs), where Technitium's logs show each device's address, or Docker's network, where every device shows as Docker's gateway. Changing it makes the container again. Installs from 1.0.0 stay on Docker's network until changed.

packages.desc: The UniFi Network Application, the controller for UniFi access points, switches and gateways, in Container Manager with MongoDB — a community package, not made by Ubiquiti or Synology. A DSM window shows your devices, their firmware and clients, the address devices inform to and how to adopt them, which ports are used, UniFi's own backups beside consistent package backups, and memory settings for small NASes.
packages.changelog:
First release. The UniFi Network Application 10.6.106 (linuxserver.io's image) with MongoDB in Container Manager — MongoDB 8.0 on processors with AVX, 4.4 on those without (many Synology Celerons), 7.0 on Linux kernels MongoDB 8.0 refuses to start on. UniFi's first-run wizard is done for you: your administrator is made at the first start with the password shown once, the country and time zone are set, autobackups are on, and UniFi is told the address your devices should inform to. A community package, not made by Ubiquiti or Synology.

The DSM window adds:
• Devices: every adopted access point, switch and gateway with its model, state, firmware (and whether an update is waiting) and clients, read by a read-only UniFi account the package makes; a DSM notification when one has been offline for 10 minutes, and when a new one waits to be adopted.
• Adopt: the inform address with a copy button, `set-inform` and the `unifi` name explained, the devices waiting, the inform host, and the ports (inform, STUN, discovery, the guest portal) — each checked against what this Synology already uses.
• Backups: UniFi's own autobackups, copied daily into the shared folder for Hyper Backup and File Station, beside the package's backups — a MongoDB dump and UniFi's data folder, taken with UniFi paused for a moment so the two match — with restore.
• Memory: Java's heap and MongoDB's cache, with suggestions for this NAS's memory and what each uses now.
• Updates: UniFi stays at a tested release; the window finds newer ones and moves to them after a backup.

Also included: HTTPS with DSM's certificate, a new password for any UniFi administrator, a redacted support report and removal.

packages.desc: Uptime Kuma, the self-hosted status monitor, in Container Manager — with a DSM window for live monitor status, DSM notifications when something goes down, one-click monitors for this Synology, outages, admin password resets, backups and updates.
packages.changelog: • The Copy button for the one-time password works when DSM is opened over plain HTTP (http://nas:5000), where browsers don't offer the clipboard API. If copying is refused, the password is selected with a Ctrl+C hint.

packages.desc: Vaultwarden password manager (Bitwarden-compatible) in Container Manager, on HTTPS with DSM's certificate, with a DSM window for the admin token, users and 2FA lockouts, sign-ups, backups, mail, updates and a clean removal.
packages.changelog:
• The Copy button for the admin token works when DSM is opened over plain HTTP (http://nas:5000), where browsers don't offer the clipboard API. If copying is refused, the token is selected with a Ctrl+C hint.
• Built on the latest chassis (volumes made with Docker Compose's labels; shared HTTPS helpers).
